skills/toil/bitbucket.md

Repositories, pull requests, comments, reviewers and build statuses on Bitbucket Data Center / Server, through REST API 1.0 (/rest/api/1.0, plus /rest/build-status/1.0 and /rest/default-reviewers/1.0). Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Bitbucket Data Center version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil calls REST API 1.0 with an HTTP access token sent as a Bearer header. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

A Bitbucket HTTP access token: in Bitbucket, your profile picture → Manage account → HTTP access tokens → Create token. Give it repository write (or admin, for create-repo) permission if you’ll use the write commands. toil sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. There is no username, password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_BITBUCKET_BASE_URLyesBitbucket server root, e.g. https://bitbucket.imagile.dev (keep any context path)
patTOIL_BITBUCKET_PATyesHTTP access token
projectTOIL_BITBUCKET_PROJECTnoDefault project key, when --project isn’t given
repoTOIL_BITBUCKET_REPOnoDefault repository slug, when --repo isn’t given
targetBranchTOIL_BITBUCKET_TARGET_BRANCHnoDefault target branch for create-pr (main when unset)
writesTOIL_BITBUCKET_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

There’s no CI fallback variable.

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_BITBUCKET_BASE_URL=https://bitbucket.imagile.dev
export TOIL_BITBUCKET_PAT=<your HTTP access token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with project, repo and targetBranch usually set once under defaults.bitbucket:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "corp-bitbucket": { "area": "bitbucket", "baseUrl": "https://bitbucket.imagile.dev", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "bitbucket": { "connection": "corp-bitbucket", "project": "PROJ", "repo": "imagile-api", "targetBranch": "develop" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add corp-bitbucket --area bitbucket (or toil connections login corp-bitbucket for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_BITBUCKET_PAT.

Where a command acts

--project <key> and --repo <slug> are group flags, accepted before or after the command (toil bitbucket --project PROJ list-prs, or toil bitbucket create-pr --project ~jdoe --repo scratch ... for a personal repository). Without them, toil reads them from the first of the workspace’s remotes on the connection’s host, of any name, trying origin first (git@<host>:PROJ/repo.git or https://<host>/scm/PROJ/repo.git; ssh:// URLs and HTTPS with a user name aren’t recognised), so a fork whose Bitbucket remote is upstream works too, then the connection’s project and repo settings. create-repo and create-prs need only a project; every other command needs both, and fails with “Could not determine Bitbucket project/repo” when either is missing. meta.context says where each came from.

Pull request and comment ids are read as whole numbers from the start of the text: 12abc is 12, and abc is sent as NaN.

Commands

Repositories and pull requests:

  • create-repo: Create a git repository in a project (--name, --description).
  • list-prs: List pull requests, every page. --state is OPEN (default), MERGED, DECLINED or ALL; --author and --reviewer take usernames; --created-after (inclusive) and --created-before (exclusive) take ISO 8601 dates and filter after fetching. A date alone is UTC midnight; a date-time without a zone is local time.
  • get-pr: Get a pull request by --id.
  • create-pr: Create a pull request (--title, --source, --target, --description, --reviewers a,b). Without --reviewers, Bitbucket’s default-reviewer conditions apply.
  • create-prs: Promote --from to --to in every repository in --repos a,b, one at a time, skipping repositories with nothing to promote. Each one reports created, nothing_to_promote or error, with counts in summary. The command succeeds even when every repository failed, so check summary.error; that case also carries a BITBUCKET_ALL_FAILED warning in meta.warnings. Its time limit is 30 minutes rather than 2, so a long batch still reports every repository. The title defaults to Promote <from> to <to>.
  • update-pr: Change --title, --description or --reviewers (which replaces the whole list). Anything not given is resent as it is now, so nothing is cleared.
  • merge-pr: Merge at the current version. --strategy is sent as Bitbucket’s merge strategy id (squash, ff; Bitbucket calls a merge commit no-ff). --delete-branch sets Bitbucket’s autoSubject and doesn’t delete the branch; the merge still succeeds, with a BITBUCKET_BRANCH_NOT_DELETED warning.
  • decline-pr: Decline at the current version.
  • current-pr: The open pull request whose source branch is the workspace’s current git branch, or null. toil git current-pr is the same command. The branch is read from .git (no git needed). With no Bitbucket connection, or one missing its pat, it succeeds with { "message": "Requires Bitbucket config. ..." } (the latter with a CONFIG_INCOMPLETE warning).

Comments (--pr <id>):

  • list-comments: Comments, oldest first, replies flattened in with parentId. --no-with-replies returns top-level comments only (replies stay nested under comments), --inline-only only file comments, --general-only only general ones.
  • add-comment: A general comment (--body).
  • add-inline-comment: A comment on a line (--file, --line, --body, --line-type ADDED|REMOVED|CONTEXT, default ADDED). The line is anchored to the new version of the file.
  • reply-comment: Reply to --comment-id (--body).
  • resolve-comment: Resolve a thread by its root --comment-id, at --comment-version (default 0; list-comments reports each comment’s version). Returns { "resolved": true }.
  • delete-comment: Delete --comment-id at --comment-version (default 0). Returns { "deleted": true }. CLI only: deletes are never exposed through MCP.

Review and builds (--pr <id>):

  • diff: data.diff is Bitbucket’s JSON diff structure as a string, not unified diff text. --file limits it to one path; --context-lines sets the context.
  • list-files: The changed paths, from one request of up to 1000 changes. An entry that Bitbucket returns as a path object comes back as that object in a JSON string.
  • approve, unapprove: Approve, or withdraw approval, as the token’s user.
  • needs-work: Mark needs-work as the token’s user, adding them as a reviewer first when they aren’t one. That addition stays if the status change then fails.
  • list-reviewers: The pull request’s reviewers and their status.
  • list-default-reviewers: The repository’s default-reviewer conditions (no --pr).
  • add-reviewer: Add --user as a reviewer.
  • list-builds: Build statuses of the pull request’s newest commit.
  • get-build-status: Build statuses of --commit <sha>. It still needs a project and repo, though it doesn’t use them.

list-builds and get-build-status return one page of statuses, at Bitbucket’s default size (25).

Write commands need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write on the call.

toil bitbucket --project PROJ --repo imagile-api list-prs --state OPEN --author jdoe
toil bitbucket get-pr --id 42
toil bitbucket create-pr --title "Add retries" --source feature/retries --allow-write
toil bitbucket list-comments --pr 42 --no-with-replies

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier: each project key it names (project, per repo or not, and projects) exists, and each repository (repo) in its project. It’s toil bitbucket check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Bitbucket server root, e.g. https://bitbucket.imagile.dev

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_BASE_URL

  • pat required secret

    HTTP access token

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_PAT

  • project

    Default project key

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_PROJECT

  • repo

    Default repository slug

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_REPO

  • targetBranch

    Default target branch for create-pr (main when unset)

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_TARGET_BRANCH
